title: The filtration definition omits the conditions needed for its valuation and truth lemma.
details: Definition 0.1 begins with an arbitrary set Σ of formulas and defines V^f(p) by the value of p at a representative for every atom p. This need not be well defined: on the two-world chain w<v with p false only at w, let Σ={p→p}. Both worlds agree on Σ but disagree on p, so their single quotient world receives inconsistent values for p. Even for subformula-closed Σ, an atom absent from Σ may distinguish equivalent worlds. Proposition 0.2 also uses induction on subformulas without assuming that Σ is subformula closed. Repair: assume a finite subformula-closed Σ; define the quotient valuation by representatives only for atoms in Σ and assign false to atoms outside Σ; ensure the chosen quotient accessibility is a persistent preorder/partial order satisfying the stated preservation conditions. Alternatively use realized canonical traces T∩Σ ordered by inclusion, with the same tracked-atom valuation, and prove the truth lemma directly. The finite-model entry uses this latter corrected construction. No upstream correction was observed. Current corpus adoption: intuitionistic-propositional-finite-model-property#finite-subformulas, intuitionistic-propositional-finite-model-property#finite-trace-model, intuitionistic-propositional-finite-model-property#bounded-truth-lemma, intuitionistic-propositional-finite-model-property#closure-and-empty-traces. The adopted closure-and-empty-traces example also isolates the closure requirement after repairing untracked values: for Σ={¬p₀}, the chain lower-world prime theory omits ¬p₀, while p₀ is untracked and false at all trace worlds, so every trace forces ¬p₀. Thus false values outside Σ alone do not establish the claimed general truth lemma.
